chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah send blessings upon him and his family) said: 'Verily Allah — there is no god except Him — surely repels through charity: disease, abscesses, burning, drowning, collapse, and madness.' And he (may Allah send blessings upon him and his family) counted seventy categories of evil.

key_terms.الدَّاء: al-da' — disease, illness, any form of sickness
key_terms.الدُّبَيْلَة: al-dubaylah — an internal abscess or boil, a painful swelling beneath the skin
key_terms.السُّوء: al-su' — evil, harm, misfortune — a comprehensive term for all forms of affliction
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: sadaqa — voluntary charity given for the sake of Allah, distinct from the obligatory zakat
key_terms.الهَدْم: al-hadm — structural collapse, falling of a building

ai.seo_question: Does charity (sadaqa) protect from disease and misfortune in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) declaration that Allah repels six named afflictions — disease, abscesses, fire, drowning, structural collapse, and madness — through the act of giving sadaqa (voluntary charity), and that in total sadaqa wards off seventy categories of evil. The hadith is transmitted through Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) via his forefathers, emphasizing the spiritual and worldly protective power of charity. The invocation of the shahada formula ('there is no god except Him') before the statement underscores that this divine protection is uniquely in Allah's hands.
